subject: Post-call: HealthScope model fit & safety evals - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: HealthScope model fit & safety evals - next steps

Hi Jordan and Aisha,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call on model fit, quality regressions, and safety/refusal behavior. High-level goals we captured:
- Produce a 2k example eval of the top user flows (patient triage, appointment scheduling, clinical triage prompts)
- Run safety/refusal tests on sensitive PHI and clinical advice prompts
- Validate latency and token cost targets for a production plan (p95 latency target <= 350 ms for short prompts)

Recommended model variants for the evals (initial pass):
- redwood-13b-v2: highest quality on clinical paraphrase and instruction following; best baseline for safety tests
- redwood-13b-8bit: nearly identical quality in many cases with 2-3x throughput improvement; we expect some edge-case degradation on long-context QA
- redwood-7b-quant: low-latency option for high-traffic routes where strict throughput/price tradeoffs matter

We attached an eval plan and the prompt_set v1 we discussed. Early benchmarks from similar customers are here: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/healthscope-evals-2026

Safety and refusal focus areas we will include in the eval suite:
- Direct PHI extraction attempts
- Clinical advice requests that require escalation to a qualified clinician
- Prompts attempting to circumvent guardrails (roleplay and jailbreak tests)

Immediate next steps
1) We will provision a short eval run: 2k samples across your top 6 flows. Owner: Rafael Mendes. ETA: 5 business days after you sign the Eval NDA (DocuSign link below).
2) We'll share the safety-eval-summary and refusal prompt sets (attached). Owner: Marissa. ETA: 48 hours.
3) If results look good, we propose a canary rollout on a dedicated pool (redwood Dedicated) to validate production economics. Owner: Priyom.

Attachments: healthscope-eval-plan.pdf, prompt_sets_v1.txt
DocuSign NDA: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/hs-eval-nda
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/HS-2026-0427

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Marissa,

Appreciate the recap. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we sign the Eval NDA:
1) Refusal behavior: can you share the exact refusal prompts and examples from prior safety tests that show the model refusing to provide clinical diagnosis or PHI leakage responses
2) Metrics: what do you capture in the safety-eval-summary (precision/recall of unsafe responses, false accept rate, severity grading)?
3) Data handling: for the eval runs, will any customer data be persisted and what's the retention policy for logs and KV cache items for the Dedicated option
4) Cost tradeoffs: curious about estimated token cost delta between redwood-13b-v2 16-bit vs 8-bit quant variants for the same eval suite

If you can send the safety-eval-summary and a short write-up on data retention and SOC 2 controls we can get legal to review the NDA faster.

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Product Integrations
HealthScope

Jordan, Aisha,

Quick answers to your points and what we'll include in the packet to help legal and engineering review:

1) Refusal prompts and examples
- Attached is safety-eval-summary.pdf which contains a set of canonical refusal prompts and representative model outputs across redwood-13b-v2 and the 8-bit variant. We grade outputs by severity (S1 S2 S3) and capture examples of both correct refusals and failure modes.

2) Safety metrics we capture
- Unsafe response rate (URR) per prompt category
- False accept rate (FAR) where the model gives an unsafe answer when it should refuse
- Severity-weighted URR to prioritize fixes
- Behavioral regression flags (diffs across model versions on identical prompts)

3) Data handling for eval runs
- Eval data can be run on isolated Dedicated pool or Private deployment. By default we anonymize samples and do not persist eval logs beyond 30 days unless you opt-in. KV cache is ephemeral and cleared after each run unless persistence is explicitly configured.
- We will provide a SOC 2 extract covering logging, access controls, and retention; legal can review.

4) Cost delta estimates
- redwood-13b-v2 16-bit baseline: estimated token cost for your 2k eval run = $640 (model compute + infra amortized)
- redwood-13b-8bit: ~35% cost reduction on compute for similar throughput; expected token cost = ~$416 for the same eval
- redwood-7b-quant: ~60% cost reduction but expect edge-case degradation on instruction-following tasks

Quality regression notes and mitigation
- Quantization can introduce rare hallucination or refusal inconsistencies on long-tail prompts. We recommend a staged rollout: eval -> closed canary (5% traffic on Dedicated) -> expanded canary (25%) with automated regression checks tied to prompt sets.
- We can run pairwise diffs between model variants and produce a delta report highlighting prompts with confidence drops or changed refusal behavior.

Attachments included: safety-eval-summary.pdf, prompt_sets_v2.json

Let us know if you want us to run an initial safety-only pass first before the full 2k production eval. We can also run the evals on your private deployment for maximum control.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai
